mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the same month as a decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.5% predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened policy expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% AND CPIAUCSL falls ≥0.5% in the same month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a no-policy change baseline (p > 0.05) in the identified tightening month, or CPIAUCSL does not fall by ≥0.5% when FEDFUNDS rises above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS of at least 2% for three consecutive months coincides with a decline in UNRATE below 5.5%, signaling labor market softening that precedes S&P 500 gains over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases ≥2% for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE falls below 5.5% in the third month
regime_hint: labor market weakening before a potential recovery
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in all months where the trigger occurs, or UNRATE does not fall below 5.5% during the three-month PAYEMS surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly surge in HOUST (industrial production) of at least 5% followed by a decline in RSAFS by 10% within the same month predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as profit expectations cool.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases ≥5% in a month AND RSAFS decreases ≥10% in the same month
failure_condition: 20 out of 20 instances of this pattern produce positive 5-day forward returns, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3% while GDPC1 rises by at least 1% indicates supply-side weakness that precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in 80% of months where INDPRO falls ≥3% and GDPC1 rises ≥1%, or the correlation with SPX is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5.25% for two consecutive months and UNRATE stays above 6%, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 60 days due to persistent policy tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE > 6% in both months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not negative in any month matching the trigger, or the effect is not robust to alternative policy rate scenarios in a stress test.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in PAYEMS exceeding 10% in a month when UNRATE is below 5% predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as hiring accelerates and wage growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases ≥10% in a month AND UNRATE < 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 80% of such trigger months, or wage growth (UNRATE) does not remain below 5% during the hiring surge.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly convergence of INDPRO and GDPC1 into a ratio below 0.9 for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as persistent supply imbalances suppress profit margins.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not negative in more than 60% of such months, or the ratio does not persist for three consecutive months in practice.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in CPIAUCSL of at least 2% in a month when FEDFUNDS is held constant suggests market anticipation of disinflation, leading to S&P 500 gains over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases ≥2% in a month AND FEDFUNDS does not change direction in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 80% of identified disinflation months, or FEDFUNDS moves in the opposite direction during the CPI drop.
